key_insight: Critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes steer gradient descent toward flatter minima while providing uniform-in-time guarantees on sharpness and loss reduction for locally quadratic objectives.
engineering_relevance: CDP offers an adaptive stepsize rule for seeking low-loss, low-sharpness solutions, with empirical flattening effects observed in neural networks and LLM fine-tuning.
method: Multiply the classical Polyak stepsize by 4 and a mild damping factor.
Use curvature-adaptive oscillations near the minimizer manifold, with damping driving convergence.
At small loss, projected iterates approximately descend log top-Hessian-eigenvalue along the minimizer manifold.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees for non-negative losses with locally quadratic Morse–Bott structure and empirical flattening similar to SAM in nonlinear teacher–student networks and pre-trained LLM fine-tuning.
watch_item: The convergence and sharpness guarantees require local Morse–Bott structure; empirical results beyond this regime do not establish the same guarantees.
paper_title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
